title: Causal Composition Diffusion Model for Closed-loop Traffic Generation

control_signal.value: User-defined reward objectives (e.g. collision guidance weight -50.0, off-road weight 1.0) and the number of controllable agents (1 to 10 or full).

control_mechanism.value: Structure-aware classifier-free guidance plus masked compositional classifier-based reward-gradient guidance; a learned causal graph ranks agents and only important ones are guided, to avoid realism-control gradient conflict.

base_model.value: DDPM-style diffusion with scene-transformer: temporal tokenizer, spatial attention giving a decision causal graph, action decoder, ResNet-18 map encoder, 100 denoising steps.

datasets.value: nuScenes and traffic behavior simulation (tbsim); trained on train split, evaluated on 100 randomly sampled validation scenes with 3 s history and 10 s generation.

metrics.value: Controllability Score from scenario collision rate; Realism Score averaging off-road rate, FDE and comfort distance; Pareto metrics GD and IGD.

controllability_evidence.value: CCDiff beats baselines on Pareto frontier; one setting IGD 0.0917 / GD 0.0617 vs CTG 0.1339 / 0.1085. Ablation: non-causal ranking costs 5 to 10 % collision rate.

stated_limitations.value: Causal reasoning pipeline relies on hyperparameter tuning and is hard to evaluate directly.

notes: GD/IGD values come from a Figure 4 table whose panel (multi-agent vs long-horizon) is ambiguous in the extracted text; the pair quoted is the first listed.
